title: Little French House
description: A fast, beautiful digital menu for an all-day café & bakery — live categories, search, dietary filters and rich item pages with nutrition and pricing.
longDescription:
Little French House replaces the printed menu with a digital one that actually helps guests order. Dishes are organised into live categories — coffee, croissants, desserts and more — with instant search, veg / non-veg filters and quick sorting by popularity or price.

Every item opens into its own detail page: photography, ratings, calories, protein, carbs and price at a glance, with a one-tap add-to-order flow. The interface switches between list and grid views and stays smooth on any phone held at the table.

It's built on Next.js with a Supabase backend handling menu data, media and real-time updates, and styled with Tailwind CSS so the experience stays fast even on slow café Wi-Fi.

title: Laxmi Multispeciality Hospital
description: A polished, trust-first website for a multispeciality hospital — clear services, doctor profiles, OPD timings and frictionless appointment booking.
longDescription:
Laxmi Multispeciality Hospital needed a digital front door that feels as reassuring as the care it provides. The site leads with clarity: departments and specialities, doctor profiles, transparent OPD timings, and an always-visible path to book an appointment.

Engineered on Next.js with Supabase powering appointment requests and content, and styled with Tailwind CSS, it loads fast on every device and is structured for strong local SEO — so patients searching for care actually find it.

Replace this with specifics from the engagement: the patient-facing goals, the booking flow, and the measurable results.

title: 4D Dish Explorer
description: An interactive "4D" dish viewer where every signature dish becomes a real, explorable 3D model — rotate it, zoom in, and preview it in AR before you order.
longDescription:
The 4D Dish Explorer turns "what does it look like?" into "I'll have that." Instead of flat photos, every signature dish is rendered as a true 3D model that guests can rotate, zoom, and even place into their own space with AR.

Each dish is annotated in 3D — ingredients like the Belgian waffle, saffron-infused ice cream or buttery croissant are pinned directly onto the model with tasting notes, alongside calories, protein, carbs and price. One tap adds it to the order; one more opens the AR view.

High-fidelity 3D assets stream through model-viewer and WebGL on a Next.js foundation, so the experience loads fast and runs smoothly on ordinary phones — no app install required.

title: HackJudge
description: An end-to-end hackathon management and judging platform — run events, manage teams and judges, score submissions and publish live leaderboards.
longDescription:
HackJudge is a complete operating system for running hackathons. Organisers create and schedule events, manage users and roles, onboard judges, register teams and collect project submissions — all from a single admin dashboard. Judges score against custom criteria, and results roll up into a controllable, publishable leaderboard.

The platform runs on Next.js, with Supabase handling authentication, the Postgres database and file / banner storage, and Tailwind CSS for a fast, consistent dark UI. Role-based access keeps admins, judges and participants each in their own tailored view.

Replace this with the story: the problem it solves for organisers, the judging model, and how far it scales.

title: Sweet Bites — Neon Bakery
description: A cinematic scroll-driven 3D showcase — a neon bakery kiosk you orbit, zoom and explore as the story unfolds section by section.
longDescription:
Sweet Bites is a pocket-sized bakery glowing at the edge of the night market — and the entire website is built around its 3D model. As you scroll, the camera glides around the kiosk: leaning into the order window, framing the cupcake neon sign, then pulling back until the shop becomes a beacon in a sleeping street.

Every section pairs a camera move with a beat of storytelling — counter light and sugar, a sign you can taste, the glow of the night market, built for the midnight rush. Scroll is the only control; the experience does the rest.

It's a demonstration of what we do for product brands: take one hero object, model it in loving detail, and choreograph motion and copy around it so visitors don't just see the product — they feel it.
